text: {"outcomes":[{"task":"task-24977981-d83c-4b5c-8bb7-8f0b2e05d256","audience":"owner","summary":"[@Investigate /compact and built-in commands](pnyx-task:task-24977981-d83c-4b5c-8bb7-8f0b2e05d256): the worker found Codex has its own compact start and compaction events, but Pnyx drops the start event and only flags completion. The worker also found that your earlier question about teaching agents to handle comments after compaction rests on a wrong premise. The inline comment note is sent only once per session, tracked in browser localStorage, not on every comment message. Main said earlier that every such message carries the note, so that needs correcting. After compaction an agent may not get the note again. The report will cover this and propose a fix. No decision is needed yet."}]}

Nothing needed from the owner."},{"task":"task-24977981-d83c-4b5c-8bb7-8f0b2e05d256","audience":"owner","summary":"Early findings from the investigation at https://github.com/ (no PR yet; the mockup is at http://127.0.0.1:4387/session/d3bcb70f5dc7da6f). Native probes show both Claude and Codex can compact and cancel, and both keep their contract afterwards. Codex rejects new input while compacting, so \"Send now\" must cancel the compaction and then send. In the probe, ordinary Claude input did not cancel its compaction. A fresh Claude session also has a gap: Pnyx puts its digest in front of /compact, so it reaches the agent as plain text. Main should decide whether to tell the owner now, since this shapes the \"Send now\" and queueing states on the mockup they are reviewing."}]}
